passage_text: Researchers conducted a randomized controlled trial to evaluate the efficacy of a novel antihypertensive drug, Hypotensol, in adults with stage 1 hypertension. The study enrolled 120 participants who were randomly assigned to either the Hypotensol group (n=60) or a placebo group (n=60). Baseline systolic and diastolic blood pressures were recorded, and participants were followed for 12 weeks. Blood pressure measurements were taken at baseline, 4 weeks, 8 weeks, and 12 weeks. The primary endpoint was the mean reduction in systolic blood pressure at 12 weeks compared to baseline. Secondary endpoints included changes in diastolic pressure, incidence of adverse events, and adherence rates. Table 1 summarizes the blood pressure data for a subset of four representative patients from the Hypotensol group. The results indicated a mean systolic reduction of 12 mmHg in the treatment group versus 3 mmHg in the placebo group. Diastolic reductions were 8 mmHg versus 2 mmHg, respectively. Adverse events were mild and comparable between groups. These findings suggest Hypotensol effectively lowers blood pressure with a favorable safety profile.
stem: What was the mean systolic blood pressure change for the four patients listed in Table 1?
explanation: Each of the four patients had a systolic BP drop from 145-150 to 133-138, a mean change of 12 mmHg.
trap: Averaging baseline or follow-up pressures instead of the changes; every listed change is −12 mmHg.

stem: Which of the following best describes the study design used to assess Hypotensol?
explanation: Participants were randomly assigned to treatment or placebo, which is the hallmark of a randomized controlled trial.
trap: Choosing an observational design because participants were followed for 12 weeks; random assignment defines an RCT.

stem: Which of the following statements is most likely to be incorrect regarding the safety profile of Hypotensol?

options.A: Adverse events were mild and comparable to placebo.
options.B: The primary endpoint was the mean reduction in systolic blood pressure at 12 weeks.
options.C: The drug caused significant dizziness in 30% of participants.

explanation: Correct: The passage says adverse events were mild and comparable between groups; it does not report that 30% of participants had significant dizziness, so C is the statement likely to be incorrect. Why the others are wrong: A) the passage states that adverse events were mild and comparable between groups. B) the passage states that the primary endpoint was the mean reduction in systolic blood pressure at 12 weeks. D) the passage concludes that Hypotensol has a favorable safety profile.
trap: Accepting a specific adverse-event rate that the passage never reports.

stem: The trial lasted 12 weeks in adults with stage 1 hypertension. Which follow-up study is most directly justified by this design?

options.A: A longer trial testing whether the systolic reduction is sustained over time
options.B: Prescribing the drug to children on the basis of the adult results alone
options.C: Dropping the placebo comparison because all four listed patients fell by 12 mmHg
options.D: Declaring effectiveness in all hypertension stages without further testing

explanation: Correct: A 12-week trial cannot show whether the 12 mmHg reduction persists, so a longer follow-up is the logical next step. Why the others are wrong: B) The trial enrolled adults only, so results do not establish safety or efficacy in children. C) Four hand-picked patients are not a basis for dropping the placebo group; placebo patients also fell by 3 mmHg. D) Only stage 1 patients were studied, so other stages need separate testing.
trap: Treating a favorable short-term result in a limited population as sufficient to extend claims beyond what was tested.
